issues.failure_explanation: In the proof of Example \ref{ex:explicit_whitney_partition}, Lemma \ref{lem:whitney_set_under_bilip_map} is invoked with \sigma = 4/(27\pi) \approx 0.047. However, Lemma \ref{lemma:whitney_covering_lemma}, on which Lemma \ref{lem:whitney_set_under_bilip_map} depends, requires \sigma > 1. The computed inequality m(P_{j,l}) \ge (4/(27\pi)) m(B_{j,l}) corresponds to the condition m(E) \ge (1/\sigma)m(B) with 1/\sigma = 4/(27\pi), hence the correct parameter is \sigma = 27\pi/4, not its reciprocal. Thus the covering-constant bound is applied outside the lemma's hypotheses as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace \sigma = 4/(27\pi) by \sigma = 27\pi/4 in the application of Lemma \ref{lem:whitney_set_under_bilip_map}.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the explicit Whitney set in Example \ref{ex:explicit_whitney_partition} does not justify its stated covering constant as written. The existence of a finite covering constant still follows after correcting the parameter, so the main frame theorems and numerical method are not invalidated.
issues.title: Reciprocal parameter error in Whitney-set covering-constant application
issues.why_classification: A single forced reciprocal correction fixes the violated hypothesis and preserves the claim with a finite covering constant; no new argument or loss of scope is needed.
